scope: All units read: text for sense and metre, translation and word glosses against the text. The text was not compared with the source page.

items.issue: mahaccittageham and mahīdevadevam were “dwelling in the great heart” and “god of the gods of earth”; the word glosses had the right sense.
items.change: Now “whose home is the heart of the great; god of the brāhmaṇas, the gods on earth”.

items.issue: kāmadohe describes the mansion; “the wish-granting cow of men” hung loose.
items.change: Now “a gleaming golden mansion that yields men their desires”.

items.issue: “the pain (of separation)” had no basis; the gloss had “afflictions of existence”.
vidhau kḷptadaṇḍān is “that punished Brahmā” (the well-known story), not “set bounds for”.
kumāra and īśasūno (“son of the Lord”) were merged into “ever-youthful lord”.
items.change: Now “O Kumāra, son of the Lord, …”.

items.issue: sahasrāṇḍabhoktā was “devourer of a thousand worlds”; bhoktṛ here is the enjoyer, i.e. ruler.
guhe is locative (“in Guha”), not an address.
items.change: Now “may all that I am be absorbed in Guha”.

items.issue: Line 2, namaśca tubhyaṃ namaḥ kukkuṭāya, is one syllable short of the metre (11 for 12). The usual text is namaśchāga tubhyaṃ, “salutation to you, O ram” (the ram is Skanda’s other mount), which fits the verse’s list: peacock, spear, ram, cock.
options: A. Emend to namaśchāga tubhyaṃ and translate “salutation to you, O ram”.
items.recommend: A: the metre proves a syllable is lost and the list wants the ram.

items.issue: Three small slips where the word glosses already have the right form: verse 16 cighrate for jighrate (“kisses, smells”); verse 20 guhaṃ for the vocative guha; verse 9 bhavatkleśa for bhavakleśa (“the afflictions of worldly existence”; bhavat- would mean “your”).
options: B. Correct only cighrate and guhaṃ.

items.issue: Last line: jaya tvaṃ pitā muktidāneśasūno. The usual text has sadā for pitā (“be ever victorious, O son of the Lord who gives liberation”); pitā, a nominative among vocatives, is awkward, and the translation has to supply “our father”.
options: A. Change to sadā and translate “Be ever victorious”.
items.recommend: A if you know the verse with sadā; otherwise B until the source is checked.
